Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge enterprisebench-corecraft · has stage: The captured CoreCraft creator article evaluates agents through a lightweight Vercel AI SDK harness with company-policy/system context and MCP schemas, permitting a tool-calling loop of up to one thousand steps.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.corecraft.agent-protocol.v2

  • The article calls a trajectory a single conversation turn with an internal tool loop; that is not the same as one tool call or a static QA example.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge enterprisebench-corecraft · evaluates: CoreCraft’s v5 paper uses expert-authored completeness, correctness, constraint and format criteria; task-level success requires all criteria, while RL training rewards the fraction of criteria satisfied as judged by an LLM.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.corecraft.rubrics.v2

  • A dense training reward is distinct from the strict end-to-end evaluation metric.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge enterprisebench-corecraft · dataset size: CoreCraft’s paper describes one thousand training tasks and one hundred fifty held-out tasks from a random split of the same environment for its GLM 4.6 training experiment.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.corecraft.training-split.v2

  • The article explicitly distinguishes this held-out evaluation slice from the current benchmark task set; the split is not a claim that the entire evolving benchmark contains exactly 1,150 tasks.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge enterprisebench-corecraft · benchmark task: CoreCraft’s v5 paper defines a fictional PC-retailer customer-support world with persistent Docker state, more than 2,500 entities across fourteen types and twenty-three MCP tools spanning queries, communications and state-changing operations.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.corecraft.world.v2

  • The entity graph and tool inventory are environment components, not additional benchmark families or real customer records.
